provisions.summary: Replaces the six defined liquor categories with four alcohol-by-volume tiers from July 1, 2026: $1.00/gal at 9.9% ABV or lower (beer, coolers, low-ABV drinks); $1.75/gal at 10% to 15% (still wine); $6.00/gal at 16% to 40% (most spirits, fortified wine); $6.50/gal above 40% (high-proof spirits).
provisions.approximation: The spec has only spirits, still wine and beer. Spirits are set to $6.00, the 16%-40% tier, which covers most spirits; spirits above 40% ABV would pay $6.50, so the estimate is slightly too low. Still wine is set to $1.75 (10%-15% tier); wine over 15% pays $6.00 and wine at 9.9% or lower pays $1.00, so the wine effect is uncertain. Beer is set to $1.00, which is above current $0.93 for beer other than draft. Coolers, now $0.85, move to $1.00; the spec has no cooler or sparkling wine category, so those changes are not captured (sparkling wine falls from $2.12 to $1.75 or $6.00 depending on ABV). Draft beer, currently $0.54, would also pay $1.00, which the spec cannot show separately, so the estimate is too low. Gaps: beverages between 9.9% and 10% and between 15% and 16% have no stated rate.
provisions.quote: (1) $1.00 per gallon on beverages 9.9 per cent alcohol by volume or lower; (2) $1.75 per gallon on beverages 10 per cent to 15 per cent alcohol by volume;

provisions.summary: Deletes the definitions of beer, cooler beverage, distilled spirits, draft beer, sparkling wine, still wine and wine, replacing them with the alcohol-by-volume categories in section 244D-4(a).
provisions.quote: "Liquor" has the same meaning as set forth in section 281-1 and includes alcohol, and the [liquor] alcohol-by-volume categories

notes: The bill takes effect upon its approval, so effective is null. But the new rates are written to apply 'On July 1, 2026, and thereafter,' a date already past as of today (2026-11-27); a reviewer should check whether to treat the rates as applying from the approval date instead. The bill's own findings frame the change as a CPI-U inflation adjustment, but the rates are stated as fixed dollar amounts, so I modeled those. Section 3 also sets a $6.50 rate on beverages above 40% ABV, and leaves 9.9%-10% and 15%-16% undefined; the spec cannot express those. Section 2 (definitions), Sections 4 and 5 (return and record-keeping by category) are administrative and not modeled. Where the revenue goes is not changed by the bill.
